summary: At Vael-Tor, Rae and Tallis witness a sealed record overwrite the current platform map with the remembered destruction of the same world. The name Atlas accompanies the image. Rae prevents Tallis from reporting it until he accepts that the archive is showing history, not a forecast.

Tyrus treats Theo's shard as ordinary contraband until frost, shadow and a fleeting reflected battlefield make the hold remember another use. Theo retrieves the shard and realizes its presence is affecting places that were never part of his own dreams.

Rae discovers that Vael-Tor's old defensive barrier is waking against an incoming refugee transport. With Jace's help she begins opening a long-seized manual release, recognizing that present infrastructure was built around a defense system whose original enemy has been forgotten.

Theo brings the shard to Adrian and demands a name for what it belonged to. Adrian retreats into denial until the shard causes the room to cast the silhouette of an enormous buried vessel. Theo realizes Adrian is not confused by the event; he is terrified of acknowledging it.

While Rae works to release the defense barrier, Mero appears in remembered form and argues that the refugee transport is an acceptable loss to preserve Vael-Tor. He recognizes Rae as someone who once participated in such choices. Rae rejects his logic and the identity he assigns her.

Ryn discovers Theo's forbidden shard and refuses passage. When the transaction glass briefly reflects a buried warship instead of the dock behind them, Ryn opens the gate simply to get Theo and the object away from him.

Vyn prepares to destroy the damaged refugee transport before it strikes Vael-Tor's awakened defense. Rae physically disables the authorization and insists they give the people aboard a chance to survive, committing herself to opening the barrier instead.

Vorken tries to take Theo's satchel. Theo's body answers with remembered combat reflexes he never learned and nearly kills the man before stopping himself. The struggle exposes the shard, and a vast warship's shadow passes over the present-day crowd before vanishing.

Rae and Jace go outside into Vael-Tor's violent storm to force the old defense barrier open. Rae stops treating her own body as expendable machinery and lets Jace share the physical burden. Together they open a path for the refugee ship.

The shard begins responding to something beneath Vael-Tor. Theo refuses Adrian's demand to hide it and asks what is buried below them. Adrian finally admits that the world was not empty when history was erased. The ground opens and the prow of an ancient dreadnought rises.

The refugee transport clears the defense barrier and lands hard on Vael-Tor. Rae, injured and exhausted, watches living passengers emerge. Jace makes her stay present with the people they saved rather than retreat into the old war's arithmetic.

Theo and Adrian face the fully emerged dreadnought dominating Vael-Tor's horizon. Theo asks what it is and why he remembers its design. Adrian finally abandons technical denial: forgetting erased the history, not the thing itself. The old war has physical mass again.
